1. The tenant reported that the rear yard debris pile (Photo No. 5) has been present for approximately three months and has increased in size over that period. The pile consists primarily of construction scrap, including lumber offcuts, drywall pieces, and a discarded vinyl window frame. The tenant stated that the debris was left by a contractor who performed roof work in May 2021 and was never removed. The property owner was not present at the time of inspection, and no written notice regarding the debris was posted on the premises.

2. The basement storage room garbage accumulation (Photo No. 8) was located in the common area adjacent to the tenant storage lockers. The accumulation included household trash bags, cardboard boxes, and what appeared to be spoiled food waste. A strong odor was present in the storage room and in the adjacent hallway. The tenant stated that the building has no scheduled trash pickup for the basement area and that the superintendent has not removed trash from this location in at least six weeks.

3. The peeling paint on the bedroom window sill (Photo No. 7) was observed on the interior surface of the sill and the lower portion of the window frame. The paint was blistered and flaking in multiple areas, and bare wood was visible. The tenant stated that the window has not been painted in the time she has lived in the unit (approximately four years). The tenant has two children under the age of six who use the bedroom.

4. The living room radiator (Photo No. 3) was cool to the touch at the time of inspection. The thermostat was set to 72°F and the tenant stated that the setting had not been changed in the past week. 5. The kitchen ceiling water stain (Photo No. 1) measured approximately 24 inches by 18 inches and was located directly above the kitchen sink. The stain was brown in color with a darkened center and a visible water ring. The stain was dry to the touch at the time of inspection. The tenant stated that the stain first appeared in early July 2021 following a heavy rainstorm and has grown slightly since that time. The tenant also stated that she has observed no active dripping from the ceiling.

6. The hallway ceiling water stain near the bathroom door (Photo No. 2) measured approximately 12 inches by 10 inches and was lighter in color than the kitchen stain. The stain was dry at the time of inspection. The tenant stated that this stain has been present for over a year and that the owner has been notified on multiple occasions. The tenant stated that the owner told her the stain was caused by a leaking pipe that had already been repaired.

7. The exposed wiring at the kitchen junction box (Photo No. 4) was observed with the cover removed. The wiring was visible and accessible from the countertop. The tenant stated that the outlet cover was removed approximately one week ago after a short circuit caused the outlet to spark. The tenant has been using an extension cord from an adjacent outlet since that time. The tenant stated that she has not reported the exposed wiring to the superintendent.

8. The stair tread on the second-to-third floor landing (Photo No. 6) was loose and moved when stepped on during inspection. One baluster was missing entirely and two were loose. The tenant stated that the loose tread has been present for approximately two months and that she has notified the superintendent twice. BCHD INSPECTION UNIT
ADDITIONAL COMMENTS, RECOMMENDATIONS, AND CORRECTIVE ACTION SCHEDULE
(Attached to and made part of Form IF-2021-045)

SECTION A – ADDITIONAL COMMENTS

1. The tenant reported that the rear yard debris pile (Photo No. 5) has been present for approximately three months and has increased in size over that period. The pile consists primarily of construction scrap, including lumber offcuts, drywall pieces, and a discarded vinyl window frame. The tenant stated that the debris was left by a contractor who performed roof work in May 2021 and was never removed. The property owner was not present at the time of inspection, and no written notice regarding the debris was posted on the premises.

2. The basement storage room garbage accumulation (Photo No. 8) was located in the common area adjacent to the tenant storage lockers. The accumulation included household trash bags, cardboard boxes, and what appeared to be spoiled food waste. A strong odor was present in the storage room and in the adjacent hallway. The tenant stated that the building has no scheduled trash pickup for the basement area and that the superintendent has not removed trash from this location in at least six weeks.

3. The peeling paint on the bedroom window sill (Photo No. 7) was observed on the interior surface of the sill and the lower portion of the window frame. The paint was blistered and flaking in multiple areas, and bare wood was visible. The tenant stated that the window has not been painted in the time she has lived in the unit (approximately four years). The tenant has two children under the age of six who use the bedroom.

4. The living room radiator (Photo No. 3) was cool to the touch at the time of inspection. The thermostat was set to 72°F and the tenant stated that the setting had not been changed in the past week. The tenant reported that the radiator has not produced consistent heat for the past two weeks and that the building superintendent has been notified twice without resolution. The tenant also stated that the radiator in the second bedroom has not functioned at all this season, but that room was not inspected as part of this visit.

5. The kitchen ceiling water stain (Photo No. 1) measured approximately 24 inches by 18 inches and was located directly above the kitchen sink. The stain was brown in color with a darkened center and a visible water ring. The stain was dry to the touch at the time of inspection. The tenant stated that the stain first appeared in early July 2021 following a heavy rainstorm and has grown slightly since that time. The tenant also stated that she has observed no active dripping from the ceiling.

6. The hallway ceiling water stain near the bathroom door (Photo No. 2) measured approximately 12 inches by 10 inches and was lighter in color than the kitchen stain. The stain was dry at the time of inspection. The tenant stated that this stain has been present for over a year and that the owner has been notified on multiple occasions. The tenant stated that the owner told her the stain was caused by a leaking pipe that had already been repaired.

7. The exposed wiring at the kitchen junction box (Photo No. 4) was observed with the cover removed. The wiring was visible and accessible from the countertop. The tenant stated that the outlet cover was removed approximately one week ago after a short circuit caused the outlet to spark. The tenant has been using an extension cord from an adjacent outlet since that time. The tenant stated that she has not reported the exposed wiring to the superintendent.

8. The stair tread on the second-to-third floor landing (Photo No. 6) was loose and moved when stepped on during inspection. One baluster was missing entirely and two were loose. The tenant stated that the loose tread has been present for approximately two months and that she has notified the superintendent twice. The tenant stated that she is concerned about her children using the stairs.
